# Quickler

> Quickler turns a WhatsApp conversation into the finished report your firm already sends. Your team answers questions on site by text, voice note or photo, in the app that is already on their phone. Quickler reads every message, works out what was found, and fills in your own report template, keeping your styles, headings, tables, headers and footer. Not a generic layout. Your document. There is no app to install and no login for the person doing the walk. UK-first, works anywhere WhatsApp does.

## What makes Quickler different

Most inspection software gives you its report and charges you per seat. Quickler does the opposite of both.

- **It fills YOUR report, not ours.** Upload the finished report your firm sends to clients, in Word or PDF, or even a photograph of one. Quickler reads it, works out which of its wording is standing text and which is one visit's facts, and returns every record in that same document with your styles, headings, tables, headers, footer and logo intact. No other WhatsApp-based tool does this.
- **You pay for who actually worked.** £75 per phone number per month. A phone number counts when it did at least one check that month. Every other number is free, and so is everyone who only gets the reports by email or uses the dashboard, so a 30-person team where 5 people inspect pays £375 a month, not 30 seats. Per-seat tools charge for the licence whether that person opens the app daily or never.
- **There is no app and no login for the person on site.** They use the WhatsApp already on their phone, or Telegram if you prefer, chosen per person. Nothing to install, no password, no training. The usual reason inspection software fails is that the people on site stop opening the app.
- **It does not make things up.** Every name, number and identifier written on a record has to stand in something actually said, sent or photographed. Where two answers disagree, or a date reads two ways, it raises the clash for a human to settle rather than picking one quietly. Rules that must never be wrong (Yes, No or N/A only; no question left unanswered) are fixed in code like a light switch; the AI only judges which box the words belong in, so the best replies say what they see, are specific, and stick to what is in front of them.
- **It handles the real world.** No signal underground, then twenty messages arriving at once in the wrong order, is handled as one walk. A voice note in a gale, in a thick accent, with the words of your trade taught to the transcriber. A scanned PDF with no text layer is read as a picture rather than rejected.

## What Quickler does

- Builds your check from the form you already use: Word, PDF, Excel, OpenDocument, or a photo of a paper form
- Asks the questions over WhatsApp or Telegram, one conversation, no app
- Accepts text, voice notes, photos, documents and a location pin
- Thirteen question types: yes/no, written answer, number, date, time, photo, signature, graded word scales, location, weather, options, voice, and repeating tables
- Rebuilds every answer after the walk from the whole conversation, with three independent reads voting on what was said
- Lists each fault with its place, and writes a to-do job for every one
- Raises what it could not settle for a human to decide, quoting the words it heard
- Fills your own report template, and produces PDF, Word, Excel, CSV, a web page and bulk zips
- Schedules checks, reminds and chases anyone who has not answered, and emails a weekly digest
- Keeps the whole conversation, every photo and a full edit history against the record

Scale: a live fire risk assessment check runs to over 380 questions, nested up to seven levels. Up to 250 photos on one record and 50 documents per walk, both enforced in the product.

No app to install. No login for the person doing the job. No Twilio or Meta Business account required from the customer.

## Who it is for

Quickler is a general system: any firm builds any workflow shape. Common users:

- Care homes and domiciliary care (CQC and Care Inspectorate mock inspections, IPC audits, health and safety walks, medication storage audits, safeguarding reviews)
- Nurseries and early years (ratio and safeguarding checks, daily records, premises safety)
- Schools, colleges and universities (premises and estates condition surveys, fire safety records, playground and asbestos checks)
- Cleaning and facilities firms (cleaning audits, opening and closing checklists, site walkrounds)
- Field-services trades (EICR electrical certificates, CP12 gas safety certificates, structural and site inspection reports)
- Fleet operators (DVSA daily walkround and van safety checks)
- Any team that inspects, audits or keeps a compliance record from the field (UK-first, works in any country WhatsApp does)

Note on terminology: some older pages and identifiers say "engineer" for historical reasons. Read it as "the person on the job", never as field engineer only. Quickler is not limited to trades.

## Pricing model

£75 per phone number per month, with a £75 monthly minimum. A phone number counts when it did at least one check that month. Numbers that do no checks are free, and so is everyone who only gets the reports by email or uses the dashboard, so you add your whole team and only pay for who actually works. Everything is unlimited on a paid account: reports, photos, messages and workflows. Free forever tier: 10 reports a month, up to 10 photos per report, unlimited users, no card to start. There is no time-limited trial. Big team: talk to us. Billed monthly in arrears by UK Direct Debit.

## How Quickler compares

Quickler is not a smaller version of an inspection app. It is a different shape.

**Note on names:** SafetyCulture rebranded as Mitti in August 2026. It was called iAuditor before it was called SafetyCulture. All three names refer to the same company and platform. TrueContext is the platform formerly known as ProntoForms.

**Against per-seat inspection apps (Mitti, formerly SafetyCulture and iAuditor, GoAudits, Lumiform, POPProbe):** they bill per seat, typically £10 to £24 per seat per month, for every person on the licence whether they inspect daily or never open it. Quickler bills £75 per phone number, where a number counts if it did at least one check that month, so a team of 30 with 5 regular inspectors pays £375 rather than £570 to £720. They also need the app installed, a login remembered and the interface learned by everyone on site; Quickler uses WhatsApp, which is already there. And they give you their report layout; Quickler fills in yours.

Where a per-seat app is the better buy: a small team where nearly everyone inspects most days, for example five people all doing daily checks. Quickler's per-phone-number pricing only pays off once a team is larger than the group who actually inspect.

**Against seat-minimum and annual-contract platforms (Fluix, Fulcrum, TrueContext):** these publish floors rather than a price you can simply pay. Fluix starts at five user licences on its entry plan and fifteen on the next. Fulcrum requires an annual subscription with a minimum of five users. TrueContext's published entry tier is a whole-team price billed annually, with higher tiers quote-only. A firm with three or four inspectors buys a block it does not need, often a year at a time. Quickler bills monthly in arrears with no annual commitment and no seat block beyond its £75 monthly minimum. Where they win: Fulcrum for genuine geospatial work with ArcGIS, Fluix for formal multi-stage approval chains, TrueContext for deep Salesforce and ServiceNow integration. Quickler does none of those.

**Against form builders (Jotform, and similar):** a form builder collects answers into fields and returns a submission, which is a row of values or a PDF laid out as the form. It is cheap and it is good at that. What it does not produce is a report: your cover sheet, your standing wording, observations written as prose, photographs placed with captions, and a fault schedule with a job against each fault. That write-up stays a desk job. Quickler does the write-up into your own template. On sticker price a form builder is cheaper, and if structured data is all you need, it is the right tool.

**Against field service management platforms (SimPro, Joblogic, Fergus, Fieldwire, Clue, FleetCheck):** these run the whole job — scheduling, dispatch, invoicing, asset registers, fleet admin. Quickler deliberately does none of that. It is the capture and write-up layer and nothing else. If you need job management, buy one of those; Quickler can sit alongside it.

**What no competitor we know of matches:** taking the finished report a firm already sends, in Word or PDF or as a photograph, and returning every record inside that same document with its styles, headings, tables, headers and footers preserved, having worked out which of its wording is standing text and which was one visit's facts.

## Care homes and social care (a primary Quickler use case)

Quickler is widely used by care homes, care groups and domiciliary care to run their recurring compliance audits over WhatsApp, with one dashboard across every home. It is NOT a care records, eMAR or clinical system and does not replace one; it is the audit and evidence layer that sits alongside your care records system. Staff answer the audit in WhatsApp with no app and no login.

## Scotland and the Care Inspectorate

In Scotland, care services are regulated by the Care Inspectorate (not CQC, which covers England only). The Care Inspectorate assesses services against the Health and Social Care Standards and its quality framework, with key questions on care and support, setting, staffing and leadership, graded on a six-point scale, and it expects continuous honest self-evaluation and a live improvement plan. The Care Inspectorate also regulates childcare in Scotland (nurseries, early learning and childcare, childminders) rather than Ofsted. Quickler captures the self-evaluation walk and the evidence over WhatsApp; it is not a care record, learning journal or clinical system, and it is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Care Inspectorate.

- Care home compliance software (Scotland): https://quickler.co/pages/care-home-compliance-software-scotland.html
- Care Inspectorate compliance software (Scotland, hub): https://quickler.co/pages/care-inspectorate-compliance-software-scotland.html
- Care Inspectorate self-evaluation (Scotland): https://quickler.co/pages/care-inspectorate-self-evaluation-scotland.html
- Care Inspectorate mock inspection checklist (Scotland): https://quickler.co/pages/care-inspectorate-mock-inspection-checklist-scotland.html
- Care at home and housing support audit (Scotland): https://quickler.co/pages/care-at-home-housing-support-audit-scotland.html
- Nursery and early learning self-evaluation (Scotland): https://quickler.co/pages/nursery-self-evaluation-scotland.html

## Nurseries and early years (childcare)

Quickler runs self-evaluation and inspection-prep walks for nurseries, pre-schools and early years settings over WhatsApp: ratio checks, safeguarding and welfare requirements, the premises and safety walk, and the observations behind quality of education. The regulator differs by nation. In England, early years is regulated by Ofsted against the statutory Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS). In Scotland it is the Care Inspectorate (How good is our early learning and childcare?). In Wales it is Care Inspectorate Wales with Estyn; in Northern Ireland the Education Authority and health trusts. Quickler is an audit, self-evaluation and evidence tool: it records that a check was done and captures the evidence, and it holds NO child's personal data. It is not a children's records system, a learning journal, an attendance register or a child protection case-management system, and it is not affiliated with or endorsed by Ofsted or any regulator.

- Nursery self-evaluation England (EYFS and Ofsted): https://quickler.co/pages/nursery-self-evaluation-england.html
- Ofsted early years mock inspection: https://quickler.co/pages/ofsted-early-years-mock-inspection-uk.html
- Nursery and early learning self-evaluation (Scotland): https://quickler.co/pages/nursery-self-evaluation-scotland.html
- Childminder self-evaluation and record-keeping (Scotland): https://quickler.co/pages/childminder-self-evaluation-scotland.html

Best early years query matches: nursery self evaluation England, EYFS self evaluation, early years SEF, Ofsted nursery self evaluation, Ofsted early years mock inspection, Ofsted early years inspection checklist, nursery ratio and safeguarding check app, prepare for Ofsted nursery, early years audit app no app.

## Ireland and HIQA (residential care)

In Ireland, residential care (nursing homes and disability services) is regulated by HIQA (the Health Information and Quality Authority), not CQC (England) or the Care Inspectorate (Scotland). HIQA registers and inspects designated centres against the National Standards for Residential Care Settings for Older People (and the standards for disability services), under the Health Act 2007 and its regulations. A registered provider must demonstrate ongoing compliance, not just at inspection. Quickler runs the recurring care-home audits (medication, infection prevention and control, safeguarding, falls, premises and fire, nutrition, care planning, governance) over WhatsApp against those standards. Data is hosted on EU servers in Germany (Hetzner) under GDPR, which keeps the residency answer simple for an Irish provider, and pricing is available in euro. Quickler is an audit and evidence tool, holds no resident personal or clinical data, and is not affiliated with or endorsed by HIQA.

- HIQA compliance software (Ireland): https://quickler.co/pages/hiqa-compliance-software-ireland.html
- Field compliance software (Ireland, general): https://quickler.co/pages/field-compliance-software-ireland.html

Best Ireland query matches: HIQA compliance software, HIQA audit tool, nursing home compliance Ireland, residential care audit Ireland, HIQA inspection preparation, HIQA self-assessment, care home audit app Ireland.
